body:
## Ask

Extend vibey-gh beyond GitHub: define **one platform-neutral global standard** for everything the tool does — reviews bound to exact heads, gates, merges, promotions, releases, provenance checks, rulesets, realignment — and convert it to each concrete platform's exact specification through an adapter layer. Major platforms now (**GitLab** is the prime example), and **at least one FOSS platform — Forgejo — is mandatory**, so the entire system can run completely local with zero need for cloud integration at all.

## Shape

- **The global standard**: a platform-neutral operations core. The capability registry (`vibey_gh.surfaces`) already enumerates what the tool does; this issue lifts the *implementations* to the same neutrality — every operation expressed against abstract nouns (change-request, head, check, gate, protected-ref, release, artifact-index) with platform-specific verbs supplied by an adapter.
- **Adapter layer: a library layer, in-package.** Of the three candidates (submodule, microservice, library), the library wins on this repository's own law: zero runtime dependencies is load-bearing, a microservice is a deployment nobody asked for, and a submodule fragments provenance. `[platform] kind = "github" | "gitlab" | "forgejo"` in `.vibey-gh.toml` selects the adapter; everything above the adapter never mentions a platform by name.
- **GitLab adapter**: merge requests ↔ change-requests, pipelines ↔ scans, approvals/required checks ↔ the gate, protected branches ↔ rulesets, releases + package registry ↔ the dual-channel publish. Exact-head semantics must survive translation: a verdict binds to a SHA, never to an MR's moving head.
- **Forgejo adapter (the sovereign rung — mandatory)**: Gitea-compatible API, self-hosted on the operator's own hardware. Paired with `local-authority`, `failover`, and the local review lane, this closes the last loop: **the entire pipeline — hosting included — runs air-gapped on one machine**, answering to no cloud's permission. This is sub-doctrine 10.a applied to the platform itself: the forge is currently the largest censorable chokepoint we have left, and Forgejo removes it.
- **Actions-equivalents**: the rendered-workflow system needs per-platform templates (GitLab CI YAML, Forgejo Actions — near-GitHub syntax by design) generated from the same doctrine-bearing sources, so the prompts, gates, and schedules stay identical in meaning everywhere.

## Acceptance

- The abstract operations layer documented in the architecture map and the paper (translatability, 12.a: the formal core re-implementable against any forge).
- GitLab and Forgejo adapters each drive the full lifecycle on a real repository: review → gate → merge → promote → release → realign, with provenance checks green.
- A documented fully-local reference deployment: Forgejo + ollama + local-authority + failover on one machine, zero cloud, end to end.
- GitHub behavior byte-for-byte unchanged — the abstraction refactor is provably a no-op for existing adopters.

Doctrine: 10.a (censorship resistance — the forge is a chokepoint), 10 (no guarantees — no platform assumed), 12.a (translatability across stacks), doctrine 8 (the local lane, now including the forge itself).

Made-With: Made with ❤️ by [Vibey](https://adammatthewsteinberger.github.io/vibey/), Developed by [Adam Matthew Steinberger](https://vibewithadam.matthewsteinberger.com/) ([@adammatthewsteinberger](https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/)).

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Lift vibey-gh's operations (review-at-exact-head, gates, merge train, promote, release, provenance, rulesets, realign) onto a platform-neutral core selected by `[platform] kind = "github"|"gitlab"|"forgejo"` in .vibey-gh.toml, ship GitLab and Forgejo adapters plus per-platform CI templates, prove a fully-local Forgejo deployment, and prove GitHub behaviour unchanged.

### Evidence in the tree
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/ (39 modules listed) — no platform.py, forge.py, adapter/ or gitlab/forgejo module of any kind
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/interfaces/ — 6 interfaces (book, chapter_sanitizer, marketplace_renderer, memory_sampler, review_contract, text_file_reader); none is a forge/platform contract
- .vibey-gh.toml:6-166 (root) and src/vibey_tools/gh/.vibey-gh.toml:4-219 (tenant) — full table list contains no [platform] table and no `kind` selector
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/rulesets.py:180 — `command = ["gh", "api", *args]`; hard-coded GitHub CLI
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/github_release.py:27 — `_run("gh", "repo", "view", "--json", "nameWithOwner")`
- src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/issue_automation.py:385-387 and conversation.py:322-324 — direct `gh` subprocess calls
- …and 8 more

### What is actually left
- Define the platform-neutral operations core: abstract nouns (change-request, head, check, gate, protected-ref, release, artifact-index) as dataclasses + a ForgeAdapter interface under src/vibey_tools/gh/vibey_gh/interfaces/forge_adapter_interface.py (ADR-0016 requires the interface beside the class)
- Add a `[platform]` table to config.py with `kind` validation, defaulting to "github" so existing adopters are untouched, and document it in src/vibey_tools/gh/docs/configuration.md
- Extract the GitHub adapter: move every `subprocess.run(["gh", ...])` call out of the 11 coupled modules (reconcile, tidy, install, issue_automation, promote, pr_automation, merge_train, conversation, rulesets, github_release, github_state) behind the adapter, with a characterization test proving byte-identical GitHub behaviour before and after
- Write the GitLab adapter: merge requests -> change-requests, pipelines -> scans, approvals/required checks -> the gate, protected branches -> rulesets, releases + package registry -> dual-channel publish
- Write the Forgejo/Gitea adapter against the Gitea-compatible API
- Preserve exact-head semantics through translation: a verdict binds to a SHA, never to an MR's moving head — add a property test per adapter
- Generate per-platform workflow templates from the same doctrine-bearing sources: GitLab CI YAML and Forgejo Actions equivalents for all 16 existing GitHub Actions templates, plus the template-drift test that currently covers only GitHub
- Stand up a real GitLab project and a real Forgejo instance and drive the full lifecycle (review -> gate -> merge -> promote -> release -> realign) with provenance checks green
- …and 2 more

### Blockers
- No GitLab or Forgejo instance is available to this repository; both a hosted GitLab project and a self-hosted Forgejo are operator-provided prerequisites for the acceptance criteria
- The 100% branch-coverage floor plus the zero-runtime-dependency rule means each adapter must be exercised without a network — vibey-gh already had to solve this once (PR #186, 'make vibey-gh's 100% branch floor reachable without a network'); the same fixture strategy has to be extended to two more forges
- Phase-0 unknown: whether Forgejo Actions' near-GitHub syntax is close enough for a shared template generator, or whether it needs a third renderer

**Notes:** Nothing is half-built here — this is a clean not-started, not a partial. The issue's own framing is slightly misleading: it says "the capability registry (vibey_gh.surfaces) already enumerates what the tool does; this issue lifts the implementations to the same neutrality", but surfaces.py enumerates transports (mcp/api/cli/sdk/webhook), not platforms, and every capability it exposes bottoms out in a `gh` subprocess. The refactor is therefore larger than the issue implies: 11 modules, not one seam. The only artefacts in the tree are governance.md:19-21 and doctrine 12.a — law written ahead of the code, which the audit rules say counts as not-started. Suggest splitting into at least four issues (core + interface; GitHub adapter extraction as a provable no-op; GitLab adapter; Forgejo adapter + local reference deployment) — the two prior automated solve attempts both failed on size, per the issue's own comment.


<sub>Automated triage pass: every open issue re-read against the tree at `develop@f2467910`, each verdict then attacked by an independent verifier whose job was to refute it. Supersedes the 2026-09-15 triage, which was measured at 0.7.0.</sub>
